question: Which of the following organisations was founded in Poona, Satara and other towns of Maharashtra that worked against Brahmanical orthodoxy and tried to reform Hinduism?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Paramahansa Mandali**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Paramahansa Mandali **was founded in Poona, Satara and other towns of Maharashtra that worked against **Brahmanical orthodoxy** and tried to reform **Hinduism**.
 
• Paramahansa Mandali, established in 1849 by Dadoba Pandurang, Durgaram Mehtaji, and their associates, was a clandestine socio-religious group headquartered in Bombay (now Mumbai).
 
• It represented the first of its kind in Maharashtra and was rooted in the belief in a singular deity, with a primary focus on challenging caste-based norms.
 
• Members of the organization pledged to disregard caste distinctions and consumed food and beverages prepared solely by individuals from lower castes during their gatherings.
 
• Dadoba Pandurang, along with outlining his principles in "Dharma Vivechan" for Manav Dharma Sabha in 1844, also articulated "Paramhansik Bramhyadharma" specifically for Paramahansa Mandali in 1848.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Brahmo Samaj **emerged during the Bengal Renaissance as the societal facet of Brahmoism, advocating for monotheism and reformist ideals.
 
• Ramakrishna Math and** Ramakrishna Mission,** situated in Belur Math, West Bengal, serve as Hindu religious, spiritual, and philanthropic organizations.
 
• Arya Samaj, a monotheistic Hindu reform movement in India, emphasizes values and practices rooted in the Vedas' infallible authority.
